title: The Science Fair and the Free Rider

pages.text: Science Fair Week had begun. In the laboratory, benches were covered with models of volcanoes, solar panels and plant experiments. Abigail’s group was building a model water filter from sand, gravel, charcoal and cloth. She had a plan, a timetable and a checklist. What she did not have was Jerome.
sentences: Science Fair Week had begun.
In the laboratory, benches were covered with models of volcanoes, solar panels and plant experiments.
Abigail’s group was building a model water filter from sand, gravel, charcoal and cloth.
She had a plan, a timetable and a checklist.
What she did not have was Jerome.
pages.alt: A school laboratory with experiments on tables and a girl with a checklist looking around.

pages.text: Jerome turned up late on Tuesday, took a photo of the model, posted it online with “my project” and left. Sandra and Sampson stayed until six to finish the filter. “Why does he always do this?” whispered Sandra. Sampson sighed. “Because nobody tells him.” Abigail looked at the checklist. Next to “Jerome”, every box was empty.

pages.alt: Three students work on a model filter at a bench while a fourth takes a photo and leaves.

pages.text: Abigail could have shouted. She could have complained to the teacher. Instead, she took a deep breath and asked Jerome to stay behind. “Jerome,” she said calmly, “I want to ask you something, not blame you. What part of the project do you want to own? We need help with the poster and the explanation.” Jerome blinked. “Nobody asked me,” he said.

pages.alt: A girl speaks calmly to a boy at the end of a day in the lab, the others watching.

pages.text: It turned out Jerome was good at diagrams and poster design but shy about speaking in front of people. Abigail gave him the poster. Sandra took the experiment. Sampson took the measurements. Abigail would present. “Everyone has a name on the project because everyone has a job,” she said. “That is fair.” Jerome nodded slowly. “I will not let you down,” he said.

pages.text: On the day of the fair, Madam Tetteh-Quao walked around with her clipboard. She asked Sandra how the filter worked, and Sandra explained it clearly. She asked Jerome about the poster, and he spoke up bravely. “Excellent teamwork,” she said. “I can see every one of you has contributed.” The group won second place. Jerome beamed.

pages.text: Afterwards, Abigail told the teacher honestly, “At first Jerome did not help, but we talked and he did well.” Madam Tetteh-Quao smiled. “Honesty is a good skill in science,” she said. “You can tell me when something goes wrong, and you can say how you fixed it. That is how scientists learn.” Abigail felt a warm glow of pride.

pages.text: Abigail wrote to her pen pal, Amelia, in another country. “Dear Amelia, I hope you are well. Last week, our school held a science fair, and my group made a model water filter. At first, one of my teammates did not take part, but we talked kindly and found a job that suited him. We won second place. What did your class do this term? I look forward to hearing from you. Yours sincerely, Abigail.”

pages.text: Exam-safe tip: Abigail wrote “you” and “your”, not “u” and “ur”. She wrote “because”, not “cos”, and “thank you”, not “tnx”. She also asked a question at the end, which keeps a letter friendly and two-way. Short, clear paragraphs make marking easier. The end.
